headline: Google Research releases Deep Review after opt-in conference-paper pilots
summary: Google Research publicly released Deep Review on Oct 14, expanding its Paper Assistant Tool from opt-in pre-submission feedback for computer-science papers into a document-review product with two free weekly reviews and API access. Google reports more than 16,000 submissions across four conference pilots, while the underlying preprint details the first two pilots and an author-run test on 26 papers with 29 documented mathematical or proof errors. The authors report 89.7% error detection against 55.2% for a Gemini 3.1 Pro zero-shot baseline, using an LLM grader audited by an author. The pilots were not part of official peer review; independent accuracy, false-positive burden and workload effects remain unmeasured.
